page: Amazon Web Services m4.xlarge is a previous-generation general-purpose EC2 instance running on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.4 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance provides 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It lacks integrated local instance storage, requiring attached network storage such as Amazon EBS, and includes no discrete graphics hardware. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect the architectural age of the Broadwell-era Xeon platform. In CPU computational metrics, the m4.xlarge registers in the lower performance quartiles, achieving a single-core Geekbench score of 976.0 and a multi-core score of 2156.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 24.01 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 21.65 GB/sec for writes. Workload tests show 1.44 million operations per second in Redis SET routines and 3.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, indicating limited throughput compared to modern hardware platforms.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m4.xlarge carries tradeoffs common to legacy instances. While its balanced compute-to-memory footprint accommodates general business workloads, modern instance families offer significantly higher instruction throughput per compute cycle and enhanced memory bandwidth for similar resource allocations. Consequently, this instance is primarily suited for steady-state legacy systems, moderate web serving, development environments, and low-intensity background jobs that do not require modern instruction extensions or high I/O throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services m4.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM on a 2.4 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor. Based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Xen hypervisor, this instance configures 2 physical cores across 4 threads. It features no local disk storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and does not include GPU acceleration. Networking is provisioned at a 1 Gbps baseline. Evaluated across standard benchmark suites, the m4.xlarge scores in the lower tiers for CPU and memory processing, achieving 2156.0 points in Geekbench multi-core and 1.44 million operations per second in Redis operations. The resource profile exhibits a typical 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, suitable for running legacy services, moderate traffic web servers, staging environments, and basic background tasks.
